text:
lauren: Heads-up: I'm proposing a tiny "mini-eval" doc example under /optimize that walks through a short SDK snippet, shows batching + KV/prefix cache effects, and calls out a simple quant-profile choice. Goal: a runnable example devs can paste into their CI. Who wants to own the code + perf numbers?

mike: I can own the Python snippet and the PR branch (docs/mini-eval-flow). I'll keep the example compact (~20 lines) and include comments for each option.

anjali: I'll run perf sweeps (seq len 32 vs 256) on rw-opt-quant-8b int8 and fp16 and paste a tiny table. Also add token-cost calc so it's repeatable.

lauren: Great. Please also add a two-line migration footnote for folks who still use legacy batch_* keys (just point to the migration guide).

sam: Found one stale link under /optimize/batching that still points to the old quant-policy article. I'll include the redirect in the PR.

jessica: Checklist for the PR: add example under examples/optimize/mini-eval.py, add tests/examples/tests/test_mini_eval.py with a fast smoke check, update nav.yml, update the qprofile docs shortlink, add a one-paragraph recommendation block (2 bullets max) about cache vs batch tradeoffs.

mike: Draft snippet (I'll paste as code block in PR):

```python
# examples/optimize/mini-eval.py (short demo)
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="$REDWOOD_KEY")
# prefer int8 for throughput, fp16 if quality matters
quant_profile = {"preferred_dtype": "int8"}
resp = client.generate(
    model="rw-opt-quant-8b",
    input="Summarize the following customer support dialog in 2 bullets:\n- ...",
    batch_options={"max_batch_latency_ms": 25, "max_batch_size": 6},
    cache={"enable_kv_prefetch": True},
    quant_profile=quant_profile
)
print(resp.text)
```

anjali: Looks good. I'll add a small results table in the PR description like: "seq32 int8: 110ms / 0.045 tokens; seq256 int8: 380ms / 0.18 tokens; seq256 fp16: 430ms / 0.22 tokens" (numbers are placeholders until I run).

lauren: Nice. Add a short note under "Recommendations" (non-prescriptive):
- use cache for many short, repeated prefixes (low latency impact, high cost savings)
- prefer larger batch for very bursty throughput where latency budgets allow
Keep it to two bullets.

sam: I'll include the link change and mention the redirect in the PR description.

jessica: Also ping @infra to sanity-check the example test (CI uses node18/pytest7 matrix). We should ensure the example's test doesn't require GPUs to run (use mocks or small smoke assertions).

infra-bot: Reminder: docs CI does not provide GPUs. Mark tests as cpu-only and use mocking for model calls.

mike: I'll mock RedwoodClient.generate in the test. Opening WIP PR now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4019 (mini-eval: batching+cache+quant). Please review inline.

lauren: Timeline: open PR today, request reviews, merge after tests & 1 review (aim for Friday). Ping here if you hit any blockers. :thumbsup:
